t: You're looking at the home of the Royal Over-Seas League, a not-for-profit institution founded in 1910. Its royal charter commits it to promoting international friendship, and that idea ties together its members around the world. The man behind it was Evelyn Wrench, a British journalist who was once editor of The Spectator. Wrench also founded the English-Speaking Union. Both bodies were set up to encourage communication and education between peoples, so this building carries a founder's belief in bringing different countries closer together.
